claims.text: First-line agents for uncomplicated cystitis in healthy non-pregnant premenopausal women
claims.quote: Nitrofurantoin, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX, where local resistance is <20%), and fosfomycin are appropriate first-line agents.

claims.text: Fluoroquinolones reserved
claims.quote: Fluoroquinolones (e.g., ciprofloxacin) should be reserved for situations in which other agents are not appropriate.

claims.text: Classic symptoms
claims.quote: Classic symptoms include dysuria, frequent voiding of small volumes, and urinary urgency.

claims.text: CDC cystitis row rests on Gupta 2011 (its reference 10); doxycycline absent from its cystitis list; pivmecillinam and gepotidacin absent
claims.quote: Gupta K, Hooton TM, Naber KG, et al. International clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of acute uncomplicated cystitis and pyelonephritis in women

claims.text: Symptoms go away within 24-48 h
claims.quote: Bladder infection symptoms most often go away within 24 to 48 hours after treatment begins.

claims.text: Kidney infection 1 week or longer
claims.quote: If you have a kidney infection, it may take 1 week or longer for symptoms to go away.

claims.text: Finish antibiotics
claims.quote: Finish all of your antibiotics, even if you feel better. If you do not finish the whole dose of medicine, the infection may return and be harder to treat later.

claims.text: Contact right away for kidney signs
claims.quote: Contact your provider right away if you have signs of a possible kidney infection, such as: Back or side pain Chills Fever Vomiting

claims.text: Kidney spread symptoms: chills and shaking, fever, side or back pain, nausea and vomiting
claims.quote: Chills and shaking or night sweats ... Fever above 101°F (38.3°C) Pain in the side, back, or groin ... Nausea and vomiting

claims.text: Symptoms come back after treatment
claims.quote: Also contact your provider if your UTI symptoms come back shortly after you have been treated with antibiotics.

claims.text: Hospital if cannot take medicine or fluids; pregnant with fever
claims.quote: You may need to go to the hospital if you are very sick and cannot take medicines by mouth or drink enough fluids. ... Are pregnant and have a fever or are otherwise ill

claims.text: Nitrofurantoin 100 mg BID x5 days, comparable to 3 days TMP-SMX
claims.quote: Nitrofurantoin monohydrate/macrocrystals (100 mg twice daily for 5 days) is an appropriate choice for therapy due to minimal resistance and propensity for collateral damage (defined above) and efficacy comparable to 3 days of trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole

claims.text: TMP-SMX 160/800 BID x3 days if resistance does not exceed 20% or strain susceptible
claims.quote: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (160/800 mg [1 doublestrength tablet] twice-daily for 3 days) is an appropriate choice for therapy ... if local resistance rates of uropathogens causing acute uncomplicated cystitis do not exceed 20%

claims.text: Fosfomycin 3 g single dose, inferior efficacy
claims.quote: Fosfomycin trometamol (3 g in a single dose) is an appropriate choice for therapy ... but it appears to have inferior efficacy compared with standard shortcourse regimens

claims.text: Fluoroquinolones highly efficacious but reserve for other uses
claims.quote: are highly efficacious in 3-day regimens (A-I) but have a propensity for collateral damage and should be reserved for important uses other than acute cystitis

claims.text: Beta-lactams incl. cefdinir only when others cannot be used; inferior efficacy and more adverse effects
claims.quote: b-Lactam agents, including amoxicillin-clavulanate, cefdinir, cefaclor, and cefpodoxime-proxetil, in 3-7-day regimens are appropriate choices for therapy when other recommended agents cannot be used

claims.text: Beta-lactams inferior efficacy and more adverse effects
claims.quote: The b-lactams generally have inferior efficacy and more adverse effects, compared with other UTI antimicrobials (B-I).

claims.text: Amoxicillin/ampicillin not for empirical treatment
claims.quote: Amoxicillin or ampicillin should not be used for empirical treatment given the relatively poor efficacy, as discussed in the 1999 guidelines [1] and the very high prevalence of antimicrobial resistance

claims.text: Estimated clinical efficacy 93/93/91% at visit closest to 5-9 days; not comparable across agents
claims.quote: Nitrofurantoin ... 93 (84-95) ... Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole ... 93 (90-100) ... Fosfomycin trometamol (3 g single-dose sachet) 91. Efficacy rates refer to cure rates on the visit closest to a 5-9-day period following treatment

claims.text: Doxycycline not among recommended agents (term absent from full text)
claims.quote: Recommendations 1-7 name nitrofurantoin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, fosfomycin, pivmecillinam, fluoroquinolones, b-lactams and amoxicillin or ampicillin; doxycycline does not appear in the document

claims.text: First-line cystitis agents
claims.quote: Prescribe fosfomycin trometamol, pivmecillinam, nitrofurantoin or nitroxoline as first-line treatment for cystitis in women.

claims.text: Doses: nitrofurantoin MR 100 mg bid 5 days; fosfomycin 3 g SD; TMP-SMX 160/800 bid 3 days if resistance <20%
claims.quote: Nitrofurantoin monohydrate/macrocrystals* | 100mg b.i.d | 5 days ... Fosfomycin trometamol | 3g SD | 1 day ... If the local resistance pattern for E. coli is < 20% ... Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole | 160/800mg b.i.d | 3 days

claims.text: Cephalosporins are alternatives; no doxycycline in cystitis table
claims.quote: **Alternatives** | Cephalosporins (e.g. cefadroxil) | 500mg b.i.d | 3 days | Or comparable

claims.text: Aminopenicillins not suitable
claims.quote: Aminopenicillins are no longer suitable for antimicrobial therapy in cystitis due to negative ecological effects, high resistance rates

claims.text: Do not use fluoroquinolones for cystitis
claims.quote: Do not use aminopenicillins or fluoroquinolones to treat cystitis.

claims.text: Not for pyelonephritis
claims.quote: Do not use nitrofurantoin, oral fosfomycin and pivmecillinam to treat pyelonephritis.

claims.text: Diagnosis from focused history and absence of vaginal discharge
claims.quote: Diagnose cystitis in women who have no other risk factors for systemic urinary tract infections based on: a focused history of lower urinary tract symptoms (dysuria, frequency and urgency); and the absence of vaginal discharge.

claims.text: Urine culture situations
claims.quote: Urine cultures should be done in the following situations: Suspected systemic urinary tract infection; Symptoms that do not resolve or recur within four weeks after completion of treatment; Women who present with atypical symptoms

claims.text: Culture in pregnancy and high resistance risk
claims.quote: Patients at high risk for infection with antimicrobial-resistant pathogens; and Pregnant women.

claims.text: Antimicrobials beat placebo
claims.quote: Clinical success for the treatment of cystitis is significantly more likely in women treated with antimicrobials than placebo.

claims.text: Recurrent: vaginal estrogen, methenamine, D-mannose weak, prophylaxis after non-antimicrobial failure
claims.quote: Use vaginal oestrogen replacement in postmenopausal women to prevent recurrent cystitis. ... Use methenamine hippurate to reduce recurrent cystitis episodes ... Use continuous or postcoital antimicrobial prophylaxis ... when non-antimicrobial interventions have failed.
